messages.content: Write a 70-word paragraph for a school assembly about why libraries still matter.

In a world full of screens, a library is still a special place. It is quiet, it is free, and it is open to everyone, whether you are rich or poor, young or old. On its shelves you can travel to old Russia, a whaling ship or a castle in the hills. A library also teaches patience, because a good book cannot be rushed. Let's use ours more often.
Write a description of an old bookshop in a busy city lane, about 100 words.

Squeezed between a mobile repair shop and a sweet stall, the old bookshop is easy to miss. Its doorway is narrow, and inside, the shelves reach right up to the ceiling. Books are stacked on the floor too, in leaning towers that look ready to fall. The air smells of dust and old paper. A ceiling fan turns slowly above the counter, where the owner, a thin man with round glasses, sits reading. He barely looks up when you enter. But if you ask for a book, he will find it in seconds, pulling it from a pile without even searching.
Please write a short appreciation note, about 60 words, from me to our office cleaner, Mr. Ramesh, who is moving back to his village.

Dear Ramesh ji,
Thank you for keeping our office clean and cheerful for so many years. You were always the first to arrive and the last to leave, and you greeted everyone with a smile. We will miss your stories about your village, but we are happy you are going home at last. We wish you peaceful days with your family.
With respect,
Kiran and the Accounts Team
Write a short paragraph, under 80 words, explaining to a 7-year-old why we can't buy every toy we see.

Money is a bit like the water in your bottle. There is only so much of it, so we have to choose carefully how to use it. Mummy and Papa need money for food, school, the house and many other things. If we buy every toy we see, there won't be enough left for important things. But if we wait and choose one special toy, we can enjoy it even more.
Tell a short story, around 120 words, about a parrot that repeats a family secret at the wrong moment.

The Banerjee family's parrot, Mithu, could repeat anything he heard twice. That was usually funny. On Sunday, however, Aunt Shobha came for lunch, and the whole family was on its best behaviour. Ma had served her famous fish curry, and everyone was praising it. Then, from his cage by the window, Mithu cleared his throat. "Shobha Mashi talks too much!" he announced in Baba's exact voice. The room went silent. Baba turned red. Ma stared at her plate. Aunt Shobha put down her spoon slowly. Then she burst out laughing so hard that she had to wipe her eyes. "Well," she said, "at least someone in this house is honest." After that, Mithu's cage was covered whenever guests came.
Describe a big joint-family Sunday lunch in about 80 words.

Sunday lunch in our joint family is never quiet. By one o'clock, eighteen people are squeezed around two tables pushed together. Chachi brings out a huge pot of biryani, and everyone cheers. The children argue over who gets the egg. Dadaji tells the same story about his army days, and we all pretend we haven't heard it before. Someone spills raita, someone laughs too loudly, and somehow, there is always room for one more plate.
I'm 22 and moving to a new city alone for my first job. Write a short diary entry, about 90 words, about my first night there.

Dear Diary,
First night in Hyderabad. My rented room smells of fresh paint and has one chair, one bed and a fan that clicks every few seconds. I ate dinner from a takeaway box while sitting on the floor. It felt strange to have no one call me for dinner or ask about my day. I almost cried while unpacking Ma's pickle jar. But then I opened the window and heard children playing downstairs. This city doesn't know me yet. Tomorrow, I start my first job.
Say thank you to my manager, Mr. Khan, for supporting me during a hard month. About 50 words. I'm Sheetal.

Dear Mr. Khan,
I want to thank you for your support this month. When things were hard, your help and encouragement made a big difference to me. I truly appreciate your patience and kindness. It made a hard month much easier, and I learnt a great deal from you.
With gratitude,
Sheetal
Write a request to my class teacher asking if I can change my seat because I cannot see the board well from the back. Around 50 words. I'm Yash of Class 8.

Dear Teacher,
I am Yash of Class 8. I am sitting in the last row, and I cannot see the board clearly. Could you please let me move to a seat nearer the front? I think it will help me follow the lessons better. Thank you very much for your kindness.
Yours sincerely,
Yash
Can you give me a short paragraph, about 80 words, on why we should say 'thank you' more often?

Saying "thank you" costs nothing, but it means so much. When we thank a person, we show that we notice what she or he did for us. It makes the other person feel respected and happy. A simple thank you to the bus driver, the shopkeeper or the cleaner can brighten their whole day. It also teaches us to be grateful for small things. If we say it every day, kindness will spread, and the world will feel a little warmer.
Email my cousin Reena in Bengaluru, asking whether I can stay with her for two nights next month during my job interview. Friendly tone, about 70 words. I'm Gita.

Subject: Can I crash at your place?

Hi Reena,
I hope you are doing well! I have an interview in Bengaluru next month, and I was wondering if I could stay with you for two nights. I promise to be a quiet guest and not to trouble you. Please tell me if it is convenient. I would love to catch up, too.
Lots of love,
Gita
Write a bedtime story, around 100 words, about a little girl who cannot sleep until her father shows her how to count the stars.

Little Riya could not sleep. She tossed and turned, and her pillow felt too warm. Her father came in and said, "Let's go to the window." They looked at the dark sky full of stars. "Let's count them, softly," he said. They began, one, two, three, and soon lost count. Riya laughed quietly. "There are too many!" Her father tucked her in. "Then count them in your dreams," he whispered. Riya closed her eyes and began to count again. Before she reached ten, she was fast asleep.
Give me a story for children, around 85 words, about a baby bird who is afraid to fly from the nest and finds the courage.

Pinky, a baby sparrow, sat at the edge of her nest and looked down. The ground was very far away. "I'll fall," she whispered. Her mother flew nearby and called, "Just spread your wings, dear." Pinky shut her eyes and jumped. For a moment, she dropped, and her tummy tickled. Then the wind caught her tiny wings, and she was flying! She saw the treetops and the sunlit river. "I am flying!" she chirped. Her mother smiled. From that day, Pinky flew every morning without fear.
Please write about 70 words in diary form for a boy who lost his first tooth today and feels both excited and a little scared.

Dear Diary,
My first tooth came out today! It was wobbly for days, and while I was eating an apple, it just fell into my hand. I was a little scared when I saw the gap, but also very excited. Everyone at home said the tooth fairy might visit. I put the tooth under my pillow before bed. I keep poking the gap with my tongue. It feels so funny!
Write an invitation, about 55 words, for my parents' 25th wedding anniversary dinner at home on Saturday at 8 pm. It is a surprise, so ask guests to arrive by 7:45. I'm their son, Dhruv.

Dear Friends and Family,
My parents are completing 25 years of marriage, and I am planning a surprise dinner at home this Saturday at 8 pm. Please arrive by 7:45, so that we are all ready before they walk in. Do keep it a secret. Your presence will make the evening special.
Dhruv
Tell me a story, about 75 words, about a small star who thinks she is too tiny to shine. End with her shining brightly.

Tara was a tiny star in a big night sky. All around her, large stars blazed, and she felt too small to matter. She hid behind a cloud and stopped trying to glow. One dark night, a lost traveller looked up, searching for a light to guide him home. Tara took a deep breath and shone with all her might. The traveller smiled and followed her light. Tara was shining brightly at last.
Please write a note, about 35 words, asking our class monitor to collect the homework notebooks while I am away at the science quiz. I'm Tara.

Dear Monitor,
I will be at the science quiz this period, so I cannot collect the homework notebooks. Could you please do it for me and give them to the teacher? Thank you so much for helping.
Tara
Invitation to a baby's naming ceremony for close relatives, on Sunday at 11 in the morning, at our home. Warm and brief, 50 words. We are Priti and Vijay.

Dear family,
We are happy to invite you to our baby's naming ceremony. It will be held at our home on Sunday at 11 am. Your blessings and your presence mean so much to us. We hope you can come and share this joyful day with us.
Priti and Vijay
Ask the school bus driver, with courtesy, to pick me up five minutes later because my mother leaves late. About 40 words. Name: Keya.

Dear Driver,
Could you please pick me up five minutes later at my stop? My mother leaves a little late, and I need that time to be ready. Thank you for your help and your patience.
Keya
A kite-flying invitation for the street's children and parents: bring your own kite, flat ground near the river, 4 pm on Sunday, snacks for everyone, from Uncle Raju. About 40 words.

Dear children and parents,
Please join us for kite flying on the flat ground near the river at 4 pm on Sunday. Bring your own kite. There will be snacks for everyone. Come and enjoy a happy evening with us.
Uncle Raju
